features.description: Read-only customer portal a tenant's Business Partner opens from a link in a sales document email and sees their quotations, orders, shipments and invoices (lists, detail, related documents, PDFs) and their outstanding balance. The portal surface, its /sws/portal/* endpoints and the etgo_portal_link table are UNCONDITIONAL; the flag gates only whether a sales quotation, order, shipment or invoice email carries the link (ETP-6209; ETP-5267 covered the invoice only), and is targeted at the ETGO_ACCOUNT email of the user sending the document. flag.$symbolsComment: Backend-only flag: no frontend symbol exists because nothing in the browser evaluates it and no key is declared in flag-keys.js. Deliberate -- see $gatingComment. The property and env-var spellings are listed because a grep for the bare key misses Openbravo.properties and the ECS task definition. Per-account enablement leaves NO grep trail in this repo at all: it is a targeting rule in the backend's hosted control plane -- Datadog Feature Flags when DD_FEATURE_FLAGS_ENABLED (dd.feature.flags.enabled) is set and dd-java-agent is loaded, else the ConfigCat dashboard when an SDK key is set (ETP-5751) -- so the registry is the only place that records where to look.

features.$gatingComment: ONE GATE: this flag, evaluated PER SENDING ACCOUNT. Default false -- no link goes out until a targeting rule on the hosted control plane (Datadog Feature Flags, or ConfigCat as the fallback) names an ETGO_ACCOUNT email. That answers 'depende del usuario logueado' (the user's words) with the flag itself rather than a second mechanism. TARGETING IS A PLATFORM CAPABILITY, NOT PORTAL CODE: GoFeatureFlags.createProvider() installs, in order (ETP-5751): the Datadog OpenFeature provider when DD_FEATURE_FLAGS_ENABLED (dd.feature.flags.enabled) is true AND dd-java-agent is loaded (the Datadog environment is DD_ENV); else the ConfigCat provider when etendo.go.configcat.sdkKey (ETGO_CONFIGCAT_SDK_KEY) resolves; else PropertiesFeatureProvider -- so any future backend flag gets per-account targeting free -- the user asked for it on those terms ('nos sirve para otras funcionalidades'). The account email is the targeting key and is also published as the 'email' attribute, LOWERCASED, which is what Datadog rules match on (their ONE_OF/MATCHES comparisons are case-sensitive and every rule value is lowercase), and, for the ConfigCat fallback, as the 'Email' attribute as stored, because ConfigCat's ContextTransformer maps the key to its identifier and only a literal 'Email' attribute to the email. Evaluation is in memory, an undefined flag resolves to the false code default, and a rule change is live with no restart on either hosted arm (ConfigCat within one poll interval). With neither hosted arm configured the flag degrades to a plain per-environment boolean: fine on a dev box (one user), but a shared environment needs Datadog (or ConfigCat) configured before it is switched on for anyone. THE IDENTITY IS THE ETGO_ACCOUNT EMAIL, NOT AD_User.email: onboarding never writes AD_User.email (InitialSetupUtility only writes username, as EtendoGoJwtDalHelper documents), so targeting the AD user's email would read null for essentially every GO user and match nobody -- PortalLinkPolicy resolves the account via GoAccountResolver instead. No account, no email, or a failed lookup means no link, never allow. THREE shapes were tried and rejected on 2026-09-10 before this one: an environment flag ANDed with a per-sender AD_Preference (nothing worked until two unrelated things were configured), the AD_Preference alone with no flag, and an etendo.go.flags.<key>.emails property allowlist in PropertiesFeatureProvider (removed because it is inert wherever an SDK key is set -- a knob that silently does nothing is the ETP-4966 shape again). This does NOT reopen targeting-key-divergence on paid-second-tenant: that divergence needs two evaluators disagreeing, and this flag is backend-only with no frontend key -- none must ever be added. But note a hosted control plane in the backend (Datadog, or ConfigCat) makes a SHARED flag newly possible, so that item must be closed before any flag is read on both ends (ETP-4966).
features.$rateLimitInfraComment: Review W6 (ETP-6209) is RESOLVED BY INFRA, with no code change -- not a deferred item. PortalRateLimiter keys on HttpServletRequest#getRemoteAddr (30/min GET /me, 30/min POST /renew, 120/min for the data reads /home and /documents*, each its own in-memory counter). Production traffic goes browser -> CloudFront -> ALB -> Tomcat, and infra added RemoteIpValve to the Tomcat image, live from the next production deploy: from then on getRemoteAddr() returns the real client IP and every portal limit is per client (before it, they counted per proxy address). A single etendo-core task runs (two briefly during a deploy), so the in-memory counters are effectively fleet-wide and reset on each deploy; scaling out would make each task count on its own. X-Portal-Token passes through CloudFront and the ALB untouched. Do not add X-Forwarded-For parsing to the portal: the valve is the one trusted place that reads it. Source: docs/plans/2026-11-11-customer-portal-sales-documents.md -- Part A implementation notes, W6.
features.$pathsComment: Owned code = the portal feature itself, which is deleted only if the FEATURE is killed. It is NOT deleted when the flag retires: the flag gates one conditional in the email contract, so shipping it unwraps that conditional and leaves every path here in place (same shape as paid-second-tenant, which kept its paths after tenant-upgrade retired). Shared touch points, NOT owned: the document-send email contracts (DefaultDocumentSendEmailContract and the four sales contracts that declare portalDocumentKind()), the EmailContract#onDelivered hook in TransactionalEmailService, AnonymousAttachmentStreamer (the session-less main-attachment path shared with the email download link, ETP-6209), runtime-routes.jsx, GoFeatureFlags, and PropertiesFeatureProvider -- the per-account targeting added there is a platform capability that outlives this flag and must not be removed with it.

deferredItems.note: The flag only decides whether NEW sends carry a link; it never closes a link already sent (the portal endpoints never read it). Where neither hosted control plane is configured it resolves through PropertiesFeatureProvider (JVM property, Openbravo.properties or ETGO_FLAG_* env var), so a change there is a deploy/restart; with Datadog Feature Flags or ConfigCat a targeting-rule change is live without a restart. INCIDENT LEVERS, in order: (1) to stop new links going out, change the flag's targeting (remove the account's rule, or turn the flag off); (2) to stop links already sent from working, deactivate their ETGO_PORTAL_LINK rows (IsActive = 'N', by ad_client_id / c_bpartner_id / record): a deactivated link answers the same 401 as an unknown one at once, needs no restart, and cannot be renewed. There is no per-BP revocation action any more (removed in ETP-6209, plan section A.6); every link also expires on its own 48 hours after its send. Recorded so nobody plans an incident response around flipping the flag alone.

features.description: Automatic bounce-pair suggestions in the bank reconciliation of PSD2-synced financial accounts in Etendo. A bounce is an outgoing bank-statement line plus the line that reverses it (same amount, opposite sign). With the flag on, the backend auto-match detects candidate pairs, the auto-match modal shows them in a 'Rechazos bancarios' section and they can be reviewed in the reconciliation panel; accepting a pair logically discards BOTH statement lines (EM_PSD2_IS_DISCARDED) and links them as a pair, and discard and restore always act on the pair. Honouring lines that are already discarded is gated too (option 2, ETP-5581): with the flag on they are excluded from the pending lists, auto-match and reconciliation (only while unmatched; a reconciled line counts as reconciled) and count as resolved; with it off Etendo behaves as before ETP-5581 and a discarded line is a plain pending line, with two declared exceptions that are not gated: the SQL-stored counters (FIN_Financial_Account.EM_ETGO_Pending_Count and FIN_BankStatement.EM_ETGO_Discarded_Count / EM_ETGO_Status; see deferredItems pending-counter-not-gated) and the statement-edit identity fix (a recreated line keeps its PSD2 transaction id and discard flag, BankStatementLineSet), which changes nothing visible with the flag off.

flag.ttlNote: PLACEHOLDER, not a commitment: end of the current quarter (Q4 2026), set on day one before any implementation exists. Revisit it once the first account is targeted, rather than letting it drift.
flag.$symbolsComment: Backend-only flag: nothing in the browser evaluates it, no key is declared in flag-keys.js, and none must be added -- the SPA reacts to what the backend answers. The constant is GoFeatureFlags.FLAG_BANK_BOUNCE_SUGGESTIONS and its one evaluator BankBounceSuggestionsFlag (com.etendoerp.go): retiring the flag is a grep for that class. The property and env-var spellings are listed because a grep for the bare key misses Openbravo.properties and the ECS task definition. The SPA's only trail is the backend answer it renders, which never names the flag: the autoMatch groups with kind: "bouncePair" (and kpis.bouncePairs), the bouncePair annotation and counts.bounce of pendingLines, and discardedCount of the statements list. StatementLineFilter is the backend switch for discarded lines. BankBounceKpiTelemetry (ETP-5581 part 3) is the bounce-pair KPI emitter (Mixpanel events backend_bank_bounce_pair_decided / _restored / backend_bank_bounce_suggestions_applied); dismissPair is the KPI-only panel action and bounceDecisions the applySuggestions body key the SPA sends for the shown-but-not-applied pairs -- both names appear in the SPA too. Per-account enablement leaves NO grep trail in either repo: it is a targeting rule in the backend's hosted control plane (Datadog Feature Flags, ConfigCat as the fallback).

features.$gatingComment: Backend implemented by ETP-5581 part 1 (evaluator: BankBounceSuggestionsFlag; toggle points in ReconciliationHandler.buildAutoMatch, buildPendingLines and applySuggestions, in BankBouncePairService.discardPair, restorePair and dismissPair (ETP-5581 part 3: the KPI-only 'No es un rechazo', 403 with the flag off, writes nothing), in every caller of StatementLineFilter (pendingLines, loadPendingLines, the LINE_DISCARDED guards of reconcileGroup / ReconciliationFlowSupport.prepareGroup / ReconciliationDifferenceSupport / ReconciliationLineTargetSupport, the statement-lines marker in BankStatementsHandler) and in BankStatementsHandler.loadStatements; the bounce-pair KPI events (BankBounceKpiTelemetry, ETP-5581 part 3) are flag-owned and only reached with the flag on: applySuggestions builds the call's Detection only when the flag is on and hands ModalDecisions.NONE otherwise, discardPair / dismissPair / restorePair emit after their own flag check. The generic changes made alongside (environment and $insert_id on every backend event, MixpanelNeoTelemetrySink / NeoTelemetryEvent, and the allowlist keys in NeoTelemetryService) are NOT flag-owned and stay on retirement; each action entry evaluates BankBounceSuggestionsFlag.isEnabled() ONCE and hands the boolean down, StatementLineFilter and the guards take it as a parameter and never read the flag); SPA implemented by ETP-5581 part 2, which never evaluates the flag: it renders the kind bouncePair groups, the bounce line state and counts.bounce only when the backend answers them. restorePair is gated like discardPair (403 BOUNCE_SUGGESTIONS_OFF): with the flag off nothing is honoured, so there is nothing to undo here, and Classic's PSD2 Restore button still works. ONE evaluator, the backend (com.etendoerp.go). Targeted PER ACCOUNT: FeatureFlagContext.forAccount(<ETGO_ACCOUNT email of the request user>), the email resolved the way PortalLinkPolicy#currentAccountEmail does (GoAccountResolver.currentAccountEmail(), admin mode, null on failure), the same shape as bp-portal-link. No account, no email or a failed lookup means the flag is OFF, never on. Default false: no account gets suggestions until a targeting rule on the hosted control plane names its email. GATED: bounce-pair detection in the auto-match answer (and therefore the 'Rechazos bancarios' section and the pair review in the reconciliation panel, which only render what the backend answers) accepting and restoring a pair, and honouring already-discarded lines at all (their exclusion from pendingLines and auto-match, counts.discarded, status=discarded, the 409 LINE_DISCARDED guards, the discarded marker of the statement lines, discardedCount and the discarded-as-resolved status of the statements list). With the flag on, only an UNMATCHED discarded line counts as discarded. NOT GATED, because they are stored and computed where no per-account flag is visible: FIN_Financial_Account.EM_ETGO_Pending_Count (ETGO_ACCOUNT_PENDING_COUNT, the Por conciliar column, its filter, the Conciliacion tab badge and the sidebar count) and FIN_BankStatement.EM_ETGO_Discarded_Count / EM_ETGO_Status (persistence events) -- see deferredItems pending-counter-not-gated. Not gated either, on purpose: a statement edit keeps the PSD2 transaction id and discard flag of a recreated line (BankStatementLineSet), which preserves PSD2's own data and changes nothing visible with the flag off. Local: etendo.go.flags.bank-bounce-suggestions / ETGO_FLAG_BANK_BOUNCE_SUGGESTIONS (Tomcat restart). DECLARED EXCEPTION (user decision): the MCP's declared actions are static, so etendo_schema / etendo_discover list discardPair, restorePair and pendingLines' status=discarded option even with the flag off; they answer 403 / are ignored exactly as on REST (com.etendoerp.go docs/neo-headless.md, section 4.12.9 'REST and MCP on the bounce-pair surface with bank-bounce-suggestions off').

features.description: Import settings of PSD2 bank-connected financial accounts in Etendo (ETP-6151). With the flag on: linking a bank account (link / createAndLink) requires, validates and stores the import-from date and the statement grouping (a stale import-to date is cleared); import-settings requires an import-from date and a valid grouping and answers a malformed date with a coded 400; the PUT/PATCH of a financial account validates the PSD2 import keys; accounts answers maxFetchInterval so the selection modal can warn about the history the bank serves; and a statement of a bank-connected account can be deleted (a processed one is reactivated and deleted in one step; posted and matched-lines statements are refused). features.description: SEPA remittances (epic ETP-3504, first task ETP-6148, from analysis ETP-6068): reuse Classic remittances (org.openbravo.module.remittance) from Etendo GO with as few new columns as possible -- none in com.etendoerp.go (an earlier iteration added FIN_FINANCIAL_ACCOUNT.EM_ETGO_ALLOW_REMITTANCE and an «Admite remesas» toggle; both were removed by a product decision). The remittance status is the remittance module's own column REM_REMITTANCE.REMITTANCE_STATUS (AD column Remittance_Status, DAL property remittanceStatus, reference REM_RemittanceStatus PE/PR/CT/PT/CP/PP/AN), added in ETP-6148 on feature/ETP-6148 and set by REM's own processes; the remittance PR must be merged and its module built before this com.etendoerp.go change is deployed (release-order dependency, see the release-order item: the module version is bumped when the module is published and GO's module.remittance floor is raised to it in the same release). Everything else is Classic data: creating a Bank financial account while the flag is on (manual create and bank-connection createAndLink) provisions lazily, per client, the In Remittance execution process, the REM_REM document type and sequence, the two remittance payment methods (CORE collection, SCT payment) and their REM_REMITTANCE_TYPE rows, marked by the type parameter ETGO_SEPA_SCHEME, and links both methods to the account; the CORE type carries Creditor_Business_Code=000 so the SEPA XML (another team) builds the creditor identifier from the organization tax ID. Also the default SEPA mandate of a customer (reusing the OBSEPAD mandate columns of C_BPARTNER) and the Remittance window with header, read-only lines and statuses (defined only, no transitions). Out of scope: due-date selection, the SEPA XML, reconciliation, returns, structured address. Backend-only flag evaluated per account. Off: Bank accounts are created without the remittance methods, every remittance-spec request answers 403 feature_disabled, the two mandate keys are silently dropped from a contacts write body (the structured-address-for-sepa precedent, never a 403), and the SPA hides the Remittance menu entry and page and the contact mandate section through capabilities.sepaRemittances (the SPA shows no creditor identifier and no schemes). The messages ship unconditionally, and REM's status column ships with REM: the flag gates behaviour, not schema.

Release order across four repos; no repo enforces it. (1) Publish org.openbravo.module.remittance with a NEW version, because republishing 5.2.0 is refused. (2) Raise com.etendoerp.go build.gradle `module.remittance` to that version. GO's CI resolves the published JAR and does not compile against RemittanceStatusUtil / remittanceStatus until then. (3) Publish schema_forge_core TWICE, or once with both: (3a) `minDate` (schema-forge-cli, and DateField `minDate` in @etendosoftware/app-shell-core), already committed on core feature/ETP-6148; (3b) a SECOND core publish with the property-path fields, strictly per-field opt-in via the decision `propertyPath` (extract-fields `adPropertyPath` / resolve-curated / generate-contract / push-to-neo / neo-writer / neo-delta) in @etendosoftware/schema-forge-cli, plus round 3: the field options `link` and `editInPlace` and the entity option `rowEdit` (resolve-curated / generate-contract / generate-frontend); without them a regen drops the Factura link, the read-only lines and the «A remesar» input. (4) Bump schema_forge package.json, tools/app-shell/package.json and package-lock.json to the release that carries BOTH (3a) and (3b); a bump to the minDate-only release is not enough. Then, on a database where com.etendoerp.go's ETGO_SF_FIELD.PROPERTY_PATH column exists (update.database), run `make regen ONLY=remittance PUSH_TO_NEO=1` and export.database: the remittance lines' path rows need that column. And therefore: if any step is skipped or done out of order, GO fails to compile (1→2), or the published validator reports F16 on remittance and a regen with the old core drops `minDate` from the generated form (3a→4), or a regen with a core without (3b) drops the ten remittance line path fields (Factura, Fecha factura, Vencimiento, Cliente, Total factura, Pendiente, Estado del recibo, and the hidden invoice, invoiceSalesTransaction and dueOutstanding) and pushes no PROPERTY_PATH rows (3b→4). (5) ETP-6247: merge com.etendoerp.automated.remittance feature/ETP-6247 into epic/ETP-3504 (the module is fixed on epic) BEFORE merging com.etendoerp.go: it adds the remittance type parameter ETAR_SETTLE_ON_DUEDATE, which GO provisions as Y, and GO's CI clones the module from source (jenkinsExtraModules.txt: the PR branch, else the epic). GO does not enforce a version floor (automated.remittance stays [3.2.0,)): with a module without the change the parameter is ignored and «Confirmar» settles the payments on the invoice date instead of the remittance due date.

USER-ACCEPTED on 2026-11-06. The Financiero template's AD_WINDOW_ACCESS to the Remittance window (FF8080812E71F7C7012E71FD0499001B) was added to the source of TemplateRoleWindowAccess / EnsureSystemRoleTemplatesScript, but the committed modulescript classes (build/classes/.../modulescript/EnsureSystemRoleTemplatesScript*.class) predate this change: they were last compiled on 2026-10-21, for ETP-5830. And therefore: the grant is not applied on tenants, and only admins see the Remittance window, until `./gradlew compile.modulescript -Dmodule=com.etendoerp.go` is run and the classes are committed. Context, not this feature's gap: the ETP-6047 Invoice Inbox grant has the same pre-existing problem.

With the flag off the MCP still advertises and returns the C_BPARTNER mandate fields (etendo_schema, etendo_get), because the NEO field configuration is not per account. The mandate keys are silently dropped from the write body (never persisted, never refused), so an agent sees fields it cannot use and, for the mandate, gets no signal that its value was ignored. And therefore: the MCP surface is not honest for accounts without the flag until the fields are hidden per capability or the flag retires.

The default mandate (identifier = tax ID, date = creation date) is applied by the backend on save only, so existing customers get it on their next save, not retroactively. And therefore: a remittance for a customer nobody has edited since the flag went on has an empty mandate until someone saves the customer.

The remittance status (the remittance module's REM_REMITTANCE.REMITTANCE_STATUS, added in ETP-6148 on feature/ETP-6148) is set by REM's own processes; settlement and return rows update it through REM_SettleProtest. An external writer of REM_REMITTANCELINE_CANCEL or REM_REMITTANCELINE_RETURN that skips REM_SettleProtest (a data-fix, a PL/SQL procedure, a future process) leaves a stale status with no error anywhere. And therefore: such a writer must go through REM_SettleProtest or recompute the status the way it does, or the open-remittance count (OPEN_STATUSES = PE, PR, CP, PP) reads the stale value.

USER-ACCEPTED on 2026-11-06 (no backfill; the PopulateRemittanceStatus module script was dropped). REM_REMITTANCE.REMITTANCE_STATUS arrives with the default PE on every remittance that existed before the column, and only one of REM's processes (process, reactivate, settle, return, or their undo) refreshes it. And therefore: an old processed or fully settled remittance shows «Pendiente» in the list, the detail pill and the status filter, and, when its remittance type is one Etendo GO provisioned (ETGO_SEPA_SCHEME marker), it counts as open (PE, PR, CP, PP) wherever Etendo GO asks whether a remittance is still open, until it goes through a REM process again (or a data-fix sets its status). The impact is installation-wide, not only Etendo GO. REMITTANCE_STATUS is NOT NULL with default 'PE', and REM adds a displayed «Remittance Status» field to the Classic Remittance window, so every REM installation, including Classic tenants without the flag, shows «Pending» on pre-existing processed or settled remittances. The cheap mitigation, an onCreateDefault of CASE WHEN PROCESSED='Y' THEN 'PR' ELSE 'PE' END for the column, was offered and declined by the user on 2026-11-06.

USER-DEFERRED on 2026-11-06 («luego vemos»). 13 new message keys exist only in com.etendoerp.go's neo_hints_{en,es}.properties, with no AD_MESSAGE row, unlike the first 15 ETGO_Remittance* keys: ETGO_RemittanceAlreadyProcessed, ETGO_RemittanceNoLines, ETGO_RemittanceProcessFailed, ETGO_RemittanceNotProcessed, ETGO_RemittanceReactivateFailed, ETGO_RemittanceDueDatePast, ETGO_RemittanceDueItemNotAvailable, ETGO_RemittanceDueItemsRequired, ETGO_RemittanceDueItemsSelectionFailed, ETGO_RemittanceTypeOrAccountMissing and the three ETGO_RemittanceName* hints. They work through NeoMessageText's catalog fallback. And therefore: they are not in the AD message catalog. Anything that resolves messages from AD_MESSAGE (Classic, OBMessageUtils, a translation pack) does not see them, and they only reach the en and es languages the properties files carry.

USER-DEFERRED on 2026-11-06. The remittance has no «Contabilizar» / «Descontabilizar» action and no posting-status (POSTED) column. Blocked by: the provisioned remittance types have ISPOSTINGALLOWED = 'N' (DocREMRemittance answers DocumentDisabled); there is no REM_Remittance_Type_Acct configuration; and the method/account link uses the upon-use values. Needs the accounting-defaults decision first. And therefore: remittances are never posted from Etendo GO. Once unblocked, the UI side is declarative: menuActions post/unpost, statusPills posted, and the posted field gated by showAccountingFields. The backend side is RemittanceHeaderHandler delegating post/unpost to DocumentPostingService.

The creditor identifier is not stored: the SEPA XML builds it from the organization tax ID and the Creditor_Business_Code parameter of the client's provisioned CORE remittance type (default 000, not Classic's ZZZ). That is one business code per client, not per account or organization, and nothing in Etendo GO lets the user change it yet. And therefore: a client that needs a different code per account or per organization cannot express it until a per-account setting is added.

There is no per-account switch and no backfill: only a Bank account CREATED while the sepa-remittances flag is on gets the two SEPA remittance payment methods (manual create and bank-connection createAndLink). A Bank account created before the feature, or while the flag was off for that user, has none, so the remittance header refuses it with 422 ETGO_RemittanceAccountNotAllowed and the Cuenta selector does not offer it. And therefore: an existing customer turned on later cannot remit from any of their existing bank accounts, and the SPA offers no way to provision one (no toggle any more); only a new account or a data-fix makes it usable. USER-DECIDED on 2026-11-11: they stay unprovisioned for now; a per-tenant data-fix only if a beta tester asks for it, and a one-off global data-fix as part of retiring the flag.

USER-ACCEPTED on 2026-11-11. On the NEO create path the Bank account is committed first and the two SEPA remittance payment methods are linked afterwards; if that link step fails, the failure is only logged and the account stays without the methods, with no retry and no repair path in the SPA or MCP. And therefore: such an account is refused by the remittance header (422 ETGO_RemittanceAccountNotAllowed) and is not offered by the Cuenta selector, exactly like a pre-feature account (see pre-feature-bank-accounts-not-provisioned); only a data-fix makes it usable. The same gap covers the type change (W1, extended on 2026-11-12): when a Bank account becomes Cash or Card, its remittance-method links are deactivated in FinancialAccountHandler.afterHandle, after the update is committed (outside a batch), so that a refused update never deactivates them; if that step fails, the failure is only logged and the non-Bank account keeps active remittance links. And therefore: Classic keeps listing the two remittance methods on that cash/card account (the remittance window does not offer it, since it is not Bank), and RemittanceMethodLinkObserver does not catch it because it only judges link writes; only a data-fix deactivates them.

RemittanceHeaderHandler answers every interactive callout of the remittance header itself (RemittanceNameCallout: the name suggestion on a dueDate or remittanceType change of a new remittance, empty for any other field), so no Classic callout of that header ever runs in GO: REM_RemittanceType_FinAccount, which works in the reverse order of the window (type -> account combo) and dereferences a cleared type, and, since ETP-6247, RemittanceSepaDefaultsCallout on FIN_Financial_Account_ID (it proposes the IBAN, creditor identifier and scheme in the Classic form; GO gets them from RemittanceHeaderWrites on create and when the account changes or the type switches collection <-> payment, and the «Datos para el fichero SEPA» block shows them from sepaFileData, so silencing it loses nothing). The contract lists that callout on financialAccount, which changes nothing: the SPA posts a callout for every ID-valued change anyway and never reads the contract's callout. And therefore: whoever adds a header callout that GO must run has to route it explicitly in RemittanceHeaderHandler.handle / RemittanceNameCallout (the callout request body names the trigger field).

The generator registers selectors for the read-only property-path fields `businessPartner` and `invoice` of the remittance lines (api.selectors entries /sws/neo/remittance/lines/selectors/businessPartner and /selectors/invoice), because they are foreignKey fields with a selector/search inputMode. NEO cannot resolve them: neither is a REM_RemittanceLine column; they are the paths paymentScheduleDetail.businessPartner and paymentScheduleDetail.invoicePaymentSchedule.invoice. Unused today: both are read-only, the grid renders businessPartner$_identifier, and invoice is a hidden field that only feeds the Factura link. And therefore: anything that later opens that selector (an inline editor, a filter widget that asks the selector, an MCP etendo_selectors call) gets an error instead of options. Follow-up: skip selector registration for propertyPath fields in the core generator (generate-frontend.js / generate-contract.js selectors), then regen remittance.

The lines grid shows a returned receipt only through its «Estado del recibo» column (payment.status RPVOID, named «Devuelto» in decisions.json); there is no per-line returned date or reason in the grid, which would need a core generator option or a per-line field. And therefore: the date and the reason of a return are visible in the «Devolver» dialog only.

«Confirmar» stays clickable while fileReadiness reports problems: DetailView has no way for a window to disable a declared process button (only displayLogicRaw, server visibility, requiresLines and requiresFieldMax), and adding one means growing DetailView.jsx plus a core generator option. The gate is in the dialog instead: it re-checks, lists the problems and keeps its own Confirmar disabled, and «Antes de confirmar» warns ahead. And therefore: a user can open the dialog only to find it blocked. Follow-up: a generic `disabledWhen` on processOverrides (DetailView + generate-frontend).
